Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a cavitary lesion in the right apex containing a mobile intracavitary mass surrounded by an air crescent, which is the classic radiographic appearance of an aspergilloma (fungus ball). This finding is consistent with patients who have pre-existing lung cavities, such as those from prior tuberculosis or bullous disease associated with connective tissue disorders like Marfan syndrome.
